chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Rayyan, who said:

I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about a person who made a bequest, but the executor did not memorize it except for one aspect from it. How should he deal with the remainder? So he (peace be upon him) signed: 'The remaining aspects, he should make them among the righteous (causes).'
ai.seo_question: What should an executor do if they forget most of the deceased's bequest?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (AS) provides a pragmatic legal solution for an executor who retains only a fragment of a will, ruling that the unspecified remainder be allocated to *al-birr* (righteousness). This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving the deceased's intent through charitable distribution when specific instructions are lost, ensuring the estate is not left in limbo. The ruling underscores the virtue of *birr* as a default category for unallocated bequests, aligning with the broader Islamic principle of maximizing good deeds in inheritance matters.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Rayyan who said,

‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> asking him about a human being who bequeathed with a bequest, but the executor did not memorise it except for one aspect from it. How should he deal with the remainder?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> signed: ‘The remaining aspect, he should make it among the righteous (causes)’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Rayyan who has narrated the following: “

I once wrote to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and asked him about a man who makes a will but the executor of the will executes only one item of it. What must he do about the other items? He (the Imam) signed the answer that said, ‘He can spend the other chapters (items) in good causes.’”
